question: Find the value of x, if $\begin{bmatrix}1&x&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&3&2\\2&5&1\\15&3&2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\\x\end{bmatrix}=0.$
explanation:
**Step 1:** Multiply the first row vector ($1 \times 3$) with the square matrix ($3 \times 3$): $$\begin{bmatrix}1&x&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&3&2\\2&5&1\\15&3&2\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1(1)+x(2)+1(15) & 1(3)+x(5)+1(3) & 1(2)+x(1)+1(2)\end{bmatrix}$$ $$= \begin{bmatrix}2x+16 & 5x+6 & x+4\end{bmatrix}$$

**Step 2:** Multiply this resulting row vector with the column vector ($3 \times 1$) on the right: $$\begin{bmatrix}2x+16 & 5x+6 & x+4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\\x\end{bmatrix} = (2x+16)(1) + (5x+6)(2) + (x+4)(x) = 0$$

**Step 3:** Expand and simplify the expression into a quadratic equation form: $$2x + 16 + 10x + 12 + x^2 + 4x = 0 \Rightarrow x^2 + 16x + 28 = 0$$

**Step 4:** Factor the quadratic polynomial: $$(x+14)(x+2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = -2 \text{ or } x = -14$$
